changelog: - **Starter skill vocabulary with aliases and adjacency** (#1816). `src/lib/skillSeed.ts` holds ~100 curated skills, each with a stable key, EN/TR/DE labels, the spellings people actually type (`ReactJS`/`React.js` → `react`, `k8s` → `kubernetes`, `Postgres` → `postgresql`, `Çevik` → `agile`) and unweighted near-neighbour links (`react` ↔ `frontend`, `docker` ↔ `devops`), grouped into 13 categories. Grown from the CV parser's `SKILL_VOCABULARY` — which every entry of is covered — plus the umbrella terms it lacked (Frontend, Backend, Full Stack, Mobile, DevOps, Data Engineering, QA/Testing, UI/UX Design, Product Management) and the composite strings that appear verbatim in real profile data (`Git / GitHub`, `Entity Framework Core`, `Generative AI / AI Tools`, `REST API / API Development`). `src/lib/skillVocabulary.ts` binds it to the one existing fold (`skillKey`) and exposes resolve/neighbour lookups; the seed module itself stays dependency-free so a plain Node script can load it. New `npm run check:skills` (in `ci.yml`) fails on a duplicated key, an alias two skills claim, a dangling or self adjacency, a missing EN/TR/DE label, a key that does not survive `skillKey()` and an alias made redundant by the entry's own key or label — none of which TypeScript can see, since every field is a `string`; `npm run test:skill-vocabulary` pins the behaviour (every spelling of React collapsing to one key, adjacency authored one-way coming out symmetric, free text resolving to `null`). Vocabulary only: no schema model, no filter rewiring and no migration of existing free-text skills (#1815/#1819/#1820).
